Pages | File | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `index.html` | Quickstart home: three-column layout — left product / section navigation tree, central step-by-step tutorial (each step: explanation + multi-language switchable code block + copy button + Test / Live markers), right-side on-this-page outline (scroll-spy highlighting); top Stripe docs nav (Docs / API reference / Search / environment switch) | | `embedded.html` | Embedded checkout variant: iframe / element integration steps for embedding into a site | | `customization.html` | Branding and customization: colors, logo, domain, email, etc. |

explored_user_goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full stripe-docs system, prioritizing the primary docs/tutorial flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_summary: The Stripe Docs clone provides a robust, interactive desktop experience with well-functioning search modals, theme toggles, and code copy mechanisms. However, the mobile experience is significantly hindered by usability barriers, including an unresponsive navigation drawer 'Close' button, broken native scrolling due to internal containers, and blocked pointer events on the search button. Feature coverage reached 40%, with a focus on evaluating cross-linking, interactive code snippets, and responsive layout adaptations.

exploration_plan.goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full stripe-docs system, prioritizing the primary docs/tutorial flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_plan.summary: The exploration will start by verifying global navigation, including the side nav, top nav, and the search dialog. It will then deep-dive into the primary 'Hosted quickstart' tutorial, interacting with code blocks (language switchers, copy buttons). Following that, it will validate the adjacent 'Embedded' and 'Customization' pages to ensure state consistency and content accuracy. Finally, it will rigorously test the mobile viewport, focusing on how the complex 3-column layout collapses and whether the identified small tap targets cause usability issues.
assumptions: The search dialog is functional and can be opened via click or the '/' shortcut.
Code blocks have interactive language switchers and copy buttons that provide feedback.
External links (e.g., to Stripe official docs or Dashboard) are marked or behave predictably, though the agent will focus primarily on local pages.
The 3-column layout (left nav, center content, right outline) collapses into a single column or uses hamburger menus on mobile.
risk_hotspots: Search dialog functionality and dismissal (keyboard vs mouse).
Code block interactions (language tabs, copy button state changes).
Scroll-spy behavior on the right-side outline (if implemented).
Small tap targets (navigation links, copy buttons, feedback buttons) on mobile viewports.
Navigation state consistency (active states in left/top nav across different pages).

phases.title: Global Navigation & Search
phases.objective: Validate top and side navigation mechanisms and the search dialog functionality.
key_checks: Click top nav links (Hosted, Embedded, Customization) to verify routing.
Click left nav links to verify routing.
Open search dialog via click on the search input/button.
Open search dialog via the '/' keyboard shortcut (if possible).
Close the search dialog via click outside or 'Esc'.
exit_criteria: Navigated successfully between local HTML pages using both top and side menus.
Search dialog opened and closed successfully.

phases.title: Core Tutorial Interactions
phases.objective: Exercise the rich interactive elements within the main tutorial content.
key_checks: Click code block language switchers (e.g., 'Node') and verify code content updates.
Click 'Copy' buttons on code blocks and look for success feedback.
Scroll through the page and observe if the right-side outline updates (scroll-spy).
Interact with feedback buttons ('Yes' / 'No') at the bottom of the page.
exit_criteria: Copy buttons clicked and feedback observed.

phases.title: Adjacent Pages Validation
phases.objective: Ensure secondary pages load correctly and maintain navigation state.
key_checks: Navigate to embedded.html and verify the active state in the left nav.
Interact with code blocks specific to embedded.html.
Navigate to customization.html and verify content loads correctly.
Check external links to 'Branding settings' for proper attributes (e.g., target='_blank').
exit_criteria: Both embedded.html and customization.html visited and core elements interacted with.

phases.title: Mobile Responsiveness & Usability
phases.objective: Evaluate layout collapse and tap target sizes on mobile.
key_checks: Verify how the left sidebar and right outline collapse (e.g., hidden behind a menu toggle).
Attempt to tap small targets flagged in the prescan (e.g., 'Copy' buttons, 'Yes'/'No' buttons, specific nav links).
Open search dialog on mobile and verify it is usable.
exit_criteria: Mobile layout verified, menu toggles exercised, and small tap targets tested for usability.

coverage_targets.pages: Visit all 3 known HTML pages (index.html, embedded.html, customization.html).
coverage_targets.features: Exercise search dialog, code block tabs/copy buttons, and navigation menus.
coverage_targets.mobile: Test responsive layout collapse and interact with flagged small tap targets on mobile.

notes: Pay special attention to the layout warnings regarding small tap targets. These should be a primary focus during the mobile evaluation phase.
Be cautious of external links (e.g., docs.stripe.com, dashboard.stripe.com) to avoid leaving the local test environment unintentionally.

findings.user_goal: Navigate documentation on a mobile device and dismiss the menu to read content.
findings.problem: The 'Close' button inside the mobile navigation drawer is unresponsive, leaving users trapped with the navigation overlay blocking the main page content.
findings.evidence: In trajectory steps 61-66, the agent noted: "The 'Close' button (ux-4) in the mobile navigation drawer is unresponsive. Clicking it does not dismiss the drawer, leaving the navigation overlay open."
findings.why_it_matters: A menu that cannot be closed completely breaks the mobile user experience, forcing users to refresh the page or abandon the site to continue reading.
findings.suggestion: Ensure the 'Close' button click event listener is correctly attached on mobile viewports and properly toggles the CSS classes controlling the navigation drawer's visibility.

findings.user_goal: Scroll through the documentation to reach content and interactive elements lower on the page.
findings.problem: The page uses an internal scrollable container rather than native document-level scrolling, which clips content on mobile viewports and prevents users from scrolling past a certain Y-axis point.
findings.evidence: Trajectory steps 67-72 report: "Scrolling on the mobile viewport failed to progress past Y=800, despite interactive theme buttons being located further down the page... indicates a potential issue with the scrollable container's CSS overflow properties."
findings.why_it_matters: Users are entirely blocked from accessing the lower half of the tutorials, effectively hiding key content like customization controls and further instructions.
findings.suggestion: Remove fixed height or `overflow: hidden` on the root `html`/`body` for mobile viewports, allowing the main document to scroll natively. Alternatively, ensure the scrollable container accurately calculates its `scrollHeight` without clipping.

findings.user_goal: Open the search dialog on a mobile device to find specific topics.
findings.problem: The search button in the top navigation cannot be clicked on mobile because a mobile header container invisibly overlaps it and intercepts pointer events.
findings.evidence: Action failure logs repeatedly show: "Click failed for Open search (press /)... <div class=\"sidebar-mobile-header\"> from <div class=\"page-layout\"> subtree intercepts pointer events."
findings.why_it_matters: Search is a primary navigation tool for technical documentation. Blocking access to it severely degrades the discoverability of content for mobile users.
findings.suggestion: Adjust the `z-index` and dimensions of `.sidebar-mobile-header` to ensure it does not invisibly overlap the `.search-box` button.

findings.user_goal: Switch the programming language for the tutorial and read the updated code snippet.
findings.problem: Clicking a language switcher causes the page to automatically scroll, but often leaves the actual updated code block below the fold, out of the user's immediate view.
findings.evidence: Steps 01-06 report: "Clicking the 'Node' language switcher updated its active state... and caused the page to scroll (y-coordinate shifted from 966 to 581), but the code block itself remained below the fold."
findings.why_it_matters: Unexpected page jumps without immediate visibility of the requested content can disorient users or make them believe the language switch failed.
findings.suggestion: If programmatic scrolling is necessary upon language selection, ensure the scroll target behavior aligns the code block itself into the center of the viewport, rather than just the top of the section.
findings.source_hint: Language switchers (Node, Python, Ruby, PHP) on index.html

findings.user_goal: Select a visual theme in the customization preview and know which one is currently active.
findings.problem: On the mobile viewport, selecting a theme (e.g., Earth or Bright) updates the preview but fails to apply a distinct active visual state to the clicked button itself.
findings.evidence: Steps 73-78 note: "Clicking the 'Bright' theme button on the mobile viewport did not produce a visible active state on the button itself, making it ambiguous whether the theme selection was registered."
findings.why_it_matters: Without an active state indicator, users lose track of which configuration option they are currently previewing, reducing clarity.
findings.suggestion: Apply a visible active/focus class (e.g., a colored border or distinct background) to the currently selected theme button on mobile, mirroring the desktop behavior, and ensure `aria-pressed="true"` is set.
findings.source_hint: Theme buttons (Stripe-like, Slate, Earth, Bright) in customization.html

findings.user_goal: Easily tap navigation links and buttons on a touchscreen device.
findings.problem: Several critical interactive elements have tap target heights well below the recommended 44px minimum for mobile usability.
findings.evidence: Layout warnings flag the home logo as "62x28px, below the 44px mobile guidance," the Stripe Checkout breadcrumb as "105x23px," and footer links as "191x26px."
findings.why_it_matters: Small touch targets lead to frustrating accidental misclicks and require precise tapping, which reduces accessibility for mobile users.
findings.suggestion: Increase the vertical padding or minimum height of header logos, breadcrumbs, and text links to ensure they provide at least a 44x44px clickable area on touchscreen devices.
